name: Northern Data Group
aka: Quake AI (since June 2026), Taiga Cloud, Ardent Data Centers
ownership: Subsidiary of RUM Group Inc. (Nasdaq: RUM), about 98%
snippet: German GPU cloud with about 22,000 NVIDIA H100 and H200 GPUs. Rumble closed its takeover in June 2026 and now runs it as Quake AI inside RUM Group.
origin: Northern Data formed in 2019 from the merger of Northern Bitcoin and the Whinstone Group, with Whinstone founder Aroosh Thillainathan as chief executive. The company began in crypto mining and hosting and later built Taiga Cloud to rent GPUs and Ardent Data Centers to run colocation sites. In 2023 Tether paid $420M for 10,000 NVIDIA H100 GPUs in a deal that also gave it 20% of Northern Data's shares. By 2025 Tether held a majority of Northern Data and about 48% of Rumble, according to the Financial Times.
today: Rumble closed its all-share exchange offer for Northern Data on June 17, 2026, with about 85.2% of the shares. Rumble then renamed itself RUM Group Inc. and combined Northern Data with Rumble Cloud in a cloud unit called Quake AI. Quake AI reports about 22,000 H100 and H200 GPUs and up to about 250 MW of energized or contracted power. On September 30, 2026, RUM Group bought another 8,256,155 Northern Data shares from Tether for a pre-funded warrant, which lifted its stake to about 98%. Northern Data raised its 2026 revenue outlook to €170M to €190M after GPU utilization reached about 85% in March 2026. Together AI signed a $270M multi-year contract for dedicated HGX B300 capacity in June 2026, and Tether committed to buy up to $150M of GPU services over two years.
platform: Taiga Cloud rents dedicated H100 and H200 clusters from European data centers, and the Quake AI site now sells the same fleet as on-demand and reserved multi-node clusters with a 3.2 Tb/s fabric. Ardent Data Centers runs facilities in Boden in Sweden, Lefdal and Kristiansand in Norway, and near Pittsburgh in Pennsylvania.
outlook: RUM Group plans a squeeze-out under German law to buy the last 2% of Northern Data shares. In August 2026 RUM Group signed a six-year GPU services contract worth up to $13.7B with an unnamed US cloud company for a site under development in Maysville, Georgia. RUM Group disclosed that it has no financing in place yet for that build. German prosecutors raided Northern Data offices in September 2025 in a VAT fraud case tied to about €500M of GPU purchases, and four people were arrested. In December 2025 the Financial Times reported that Northern Data sold its Peak Mining unit for up to $200M to companies controlled by Tether executives.

name: Genesis Cloud
aka: Genesis Cloud GmbH (in liquidation), team now part of Volta
ownership: Team and technology acquired by Volta in 2026, German operating company in liquidation
snippet: Munich GPU cloud that ran from 2018. In 2026 London-based Volta acquired its team and software stack, and the German operating company is in liquidation.
origin: Genesis Cloud started in 2018 and ran one of Europe's earliest GPU-first public clouds, serving more than 20,000 users, according to Andreessen Horowitz. It operated renewable-powered data centers and sold GPU capacity to European companies that wanted AI workloads under EU rules. Its later lineup included H100 SXM5 nodes with 3.2 Tbps InfiniBand, H200 and B200.
today: Volta, a London AI infrastructure startup founded in 2026 by former Brookfield executives Ricard Boada and Sofia Gumuzio, acquired the Genesis Cloud team and technology earlier in 2026. The deal gave Volta a software stack for public AI cloud and bare metal cluster management. An archived copy of the Genesis Cloud website from March 2026 names the operator as Genesis Cloud GmbH i.L., the German abbreviation for a company in liquidation. Volta came out of stealth in August 2026 with about $300M in seed and Series A funding at a $2.4B valuation. It announced a $10B partnership for a 133 MW NVIDIA Vera Rubin deployment in Norway, developed with Bitdeer, and Bloomberg reported that the customer is Anthropic.
platform: Genesis Cloud built Kubernetes-native software for GPU provisioning and production cluster management, and Volta now uses that software as its cloud layer. The service offered GPU instances and multi-node clusters on NVIDIA reference architectures, with no ingress or egress fees on storage.
outlook: Genesis Cloud no longer operates as an independent provider, so capacity built by this team now appears under the Volta name. Volta pairs cloud operations with a $5B infrastructure financing program run with Azora. It says it targets multi-gigawatt deployments by 2030.

name: Ori
aka: Ori Industries, Ori Global AI Cloud, now part of Radiant
ownership: Merged into Radiant, a Brookfield portfolio company (February 2026)
snippet: London GPU cloud that merged into Brookfield's Radiant in February 2026. Ori's software and team now run Radiant's cloud, which draws on Brookfield's $100B AI infrastructure program.

facts.label: Power deal
facts.value: $5B Bloom Energy framework, up to 1 GW

origin: Mahdi Yahya, a former telecom executive, founded Ori in London and spent more than seven years building software to deploy and run distributed cloud infrastructure for telecom operators and corporates. Ori then bought NVIDIA GPUs, placed them in leased data center space and rented them to technology companies through the Ori Global AI Cloud. Saudi Aramco's venture arm was among its backers.
today: Brookfield launched Radiant in January 2026 as a vertically integrated AI infrastructure company and merged it with Ori in February 2026. Yahya became Radiant's president, and Brookfield managing director Vishal Padiyar became executive chair. Reuters reported that the merger valued Radiant at $1.3B, and all of Ori's existing investors rolled their stakes into the new company. Radiant is the first compute deployment vehicle of the $10B Brookfield AI Infrastructure Fund, which anchors a $100B AI infrastructure program. Its first planned facilities are in Qatar, France and Sweden. By June 2026 Radiant had signed contracts longer than five years, according to ION Analytics.
platform: Radiant runs Ori's software as FlightDeck, one control layer for bare metal, GPU instances, managed Kubernetes and managed Slurm on a shared fleet. Ori's services also cover inference, fine-tuning, model registries and storage. Radiant is an NVIDIA Cloud Partner and builds clusters to the NVIDIA DSX reference design, offering GB300 NVL72 racks and Hopper systems now and Vera Rubin NVL72 when available.
outlook: Radiant plans to own the full chain of land, power, data centers and compute, using powered sites from Brookfield portfolio companies with access to more than 45 GW of renewable generation. Brookfield has a $5B framework with Bloom Energy for up to 1 GW of behind-the-meter power. Radiant targets sovereign governments, large enterprises and telecom operators. It has not disclosed GPU counts, operating sites or customer names.

name: Evroc
snippet: Swedish sovereign cloud that is building its own AI data centers near Stockholm and Cannes. In July 2026 the Swedish Armed Forces picked it to host their combat cloud platform.

facts.label: Long-term plan
facts.value: Eight data centers in the EU

origin: Mattias Åström founded Evroc in Stockholm in 2022 to build a European-owned hyperscale cloud as an alternative to US providers. The company published its plan in June 2023 and started service from colocation sites in Stockholm and Paris, adding Frankfurt in 2025. It designs its own liquid-cooled facilities for dense AI racks.
today: Evroc raised €50.6M ($55M) in a Series A in March 2025 from blisce/, EQT Ventures, Norrsken VC and Giant Ventures. It launched its cloud platform in July 2025 and sells compute, storage, networking and AI services to defense, government, finance and healthcare customers. In July 2026 the Swedish Armed Forces and the Swedish Defence Materiel Administration selected Evroc to build the cloud platform for the Swedish Interoperable Combat Cloud, which handles NATO Restricted information. Evroc began offering SUSE Linux and certified SUSE Rancher Prime Kubernetes in early 2026. In September 2026 it partnered with Vilja to bring agentic AI to European banks.
platform: Evroc runs its own cloud software on its own hardware and keeps data, control planes and support inside Europe. Its AI products include roc, an enterprise AI service, along with AI services for coding agents and banking that keep data in Europe. Its flagship Stockholm data center targets rack densities above 150 kW with liquid cooling and fossil-free power, and Evroc plans an NVIDIA Blackwell GPU cluster there.
outlook: Evroc plans an AI factory in Mougins near Cannes of up to 96 MW and 50,000 GPUs, and a €600M site at Arlandastad north of Stockholm for up to 16,000 GPUs from the second half of 2026. It aims for eight data centers across the EU. The company said in 2025 that it planned to raise more capital to fund these builds.

name: Nebul
snippet: Dutch sovereign AI cloud and NVIDIA Elite cloud partner focused on private inference for European healthcare, government and enterprise customers.

facts.label: Recognition
facts.value: 2025 Gartner Cool Vendor, AI specialty clouds

origin: Nebul grew out of high-performance computing and data center operations rather than crypto mining, and CEO Arnold Juffer is a serial entrepreneur. The company built a platform for private and sovereign AI with an emphasis on inference. It chose NetApp AFF A90 storage in 2024 after testing several vendors for multi-tenant performance, and it hosts its systems with Dutch data center partners Eurofiber, NorthC and Switch Datacenters.
today: Nebul sells a European AI cloud that keeps data under EU control and complies with GDPR, the EU AI Act and NIS2. It is an NVIDIA Elite Cloud Service Provider and runs NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs in green-energy data centers. Gartner named it a 2025 Cool Vendor among AI specialty cloud providers. In February 2026 it began offering Speedata Analytics Processing Units for Apache Spark workloads, the first cloud to do so. In July 2026 it announced a proof of concept with DDN and NVIDIA on KV cache acceleration for inference.
platform: Nebul sells its stack in three layers, with AI Studio for retrieval, guardrails and observability, an AI Engine for curated models, serverless and dedicated inference, fine-tuning and training, and a NeoCloud layer for cloud GPUs, clusters, on-premises AI pods, Kubernetes, databases and storage. Customers can run open models such as DeepSeek on the platform without sending data outside Europe.
outlook: Nebul has not published GPU counts, funding or named customers. It joined the Open Cloud Alliance on digital sovereignty and targets European organizations that must keep AI data inside national borders.

name: Deutsche Telekom Industrial AI Cloud
aka: Telekom AI Factory, Industrial AI Cloud with NVIDIA
ownership: Business of Deutsche Telekom (XETRA: DTE), operated with T-Systems
snippet: Deutsche Telekom's NVIDIA-based AI factory in Munich, opened in February 2026 with nearly 10,000 Blackwell GPUs for German industry, research and government.
customers: German Federal Ministry for Digitalization and State Modernization
origin: Deutsche Telekom and NVIDIA announced the Industrial AI Cloud on November 4, 2025, as a sovereign AI platform for German and European industry. Telekom budgeted about €1B for the project. SAP supplies the software backbone, Siemens brings its industrial simulation portfolio, and data center partner Polarise hosts the system in Munich.
today: The AI factory opened on February 4, 2026, in Munich's Tucherpark with nearly 10,000 NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs in DGX B200 systems and RTX PRO servers. Telekom rates it at up to 0.5 exaflops. More than a third of the capacity was running at launch, and early users include Agile Robots and PhysicsX. A German AI Association consortium trained the open Soofi S model there between March and May 2026 on up to 512 B200 GPUs. In May 2026 Telekom and SAP won a €250M federal contract to build a sovereign AI platform for public administration on this compute.
platform: Customers book GPU capacity from pilots through production under German data protection and security rules, and T-Systems runs the service. The software stack includes NVIDIA AI Enterprise, Omniverse for digital twins and Isaac for robotics, and SAP builds its Deutschland-Stack platform layer on top. The facility runs on renewable power, cools with water from the Eisbach and feeds waste heat into the Tucherpark district heating network.
outlook: Deutsche Telekom is pursuing an EU AI gigafactory bid, and Light Reading reported in December 2025 that it was shaping that bid with the Schwarz Group. The EU opened formal gigafactory bidding in July 2026. Telekom has not published revenue, utilization or pricing for the Munich cloud.

name: SoftBank Corp.
aka: SoftBank AI Data Center GPU Cloud, SB Neo (US)
ownership: Public (TSE: 9434), about 40% owned by SoftBank Group Corp.
snippet: Japanese telco that runs one of Japan's largest NVIDIA fleets. It plans commercial launch of its GB200 NVL72 GPU cloud in October 2026 and a US neocloud, SB Neo.

facts.label: SB Neo target
facts.value: 10 GW scale, service from FY to March 2028

origin: SoftBank Corp., the listed telecom subsidiary of SoftBank Group, built an in-house AI computing platform to train Japanese large language models through its unit SB Intuitions. By July 2025 the platform passed 10,000 GPUs and 13.7 exaflops. It includes a DGX SuperPOD with more than 4,000 Blackwell GPUs, which SoftBank describes as the largest built with DGX B200 systems. SB Intuitions uses it for the Sarashina model family, including a model of about 460B parameters.
today: SoftBank Corp. opened a beta of its AI Data Center GPU Cloud on May 27, 2026, for group companies and plans commercial service in October 2026. The service runs on NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 systems in Japanese data centers and keeps compute and data in Japan. On July 2, 2026, SoftBank Corp. and SoftBank Group formed SB Neo, owned 51% and 49%, to offer neocloud services in the United States from the fiscal year ending March 2028 at up to 10 GW of capacity. In April 2026 Microsoft announced that SoftBank and Sakura Internet will offer GPU compute through Azure with data kept in Japan. Yaskawa Electric used the GPU cloud for a physical AI robot demonstration in July 2026.
platform: SoftBank's Infrinia AI Cloud OS manages the stack from BIOS through multi-tenant Kubernetes and exposes Kubernetes as a Service and Inference as a Service through APIs. The GPU cloud uses NVIDIA BlueField-3 DPUs and Spectrum Ethernet switches, and one GPU pool serves both training and inference. SoftBank ties the cloud to AITRAS, its AI-RAN platform, under a Telco AI Cloud plan announced in March 2026.
outlook: SoftBank is building the Hokkaido Tomakomai AI data center, which it plans to open in the fiscal year ending March 2027. It plans one of Japan's largest AI data centers at its Osaka Sakai site and will start building GPU servers there in fiscal 2027. Its parent SoftBank Group owns 40% of the Stargate venture with OpenAI, and SB Neo plans to draw on energy and compute resources that SoftBank Group and its affiliates develop.

name: Sakura Internet
aka: SAKURA internet Inc., Koukaryoku GPU cloud, SAKURAONE
snippet: Osaka cloud and hosting provider that runs Japan's state-subsidized Koukaryoku GPU cloud, with a plan for about 10,000 GPUs and Government Cloud status.
origin: Kunihiro Tanaka founded Sakura Internet in 1996, and it grew into a domestic provider of rental servers, VPS, public cloud and data centers, including a campus in Ishikari, Hokkaido. In June 2023 it committed ¥13B to a first GPU cluster of about 2,000 GPUs for its Koukaryoku cloud. In April 2024 Japan's government granted it a subsidy of up to ¥50.1B, and Sakura raised its plan to about 10,000 GPUs and about ¥100B of investment by March 2028.
today: Sakura reported revenue of ¥35.3B for the year to March 2026, with GPU infrastructure services at ¥8.14B. It posted an operating loss of ¥403.7M after a ¥4.15B profit the year before. It forecasts ¥45B in sales for the year to March 2027 and is expanding Koukaryoku from about 2,000 to nearly 4,000 Hopper GPUs while adding Blackwell systems in Ishikari. A national institution ordered about ¥3.8B of generative AI compute on its SAKURAONE managed H100 and H200 clusters through March 2027. In March 2026 Sakura met all 305 technical requirements and was confirmed as a Government Cloud provider. In April 2026 Microsoft named Sakura and SoftBank as partners to offer domestic GPU compute through Azure.
platform: Koukaryoku rents NVIDIA GPU servers as bare metal and virtual machines. SAKURAONE is a managed supercomputer built on HGX B200 systems with direct liquid cooling, and in June 2026 it reached 37.79 PFLOPS on LINPACK, ranking 63rd on the TOP500 and 22nd on HPCG. Sakura also runs the SAKURA Gen AI Platform, a managed service for generative AI applications launched in August 2025.
outlook: Sakura plans to reach about 10,800 GPUs in its high-performance AI computing service and has told investors it expects more data center spending. In August 2025 it signed a basic agreement with KDDI and Highreso to meet GPU demand. In August 2026 it disclosed a breach of its sales management system that may affect up to 1.36 million member accounts. The breach hit customer contract records, not its infrastructure services.

name: E2E Networks
ownership: Public (NSE: E2E), Larsen & Toubro holds about 21%
snippet: NSE-listed Indian GPU cloud backed by L&T. Q1 FY27 revenue rose 334% after a 1,024-GPU B200 cluster went live, and it signed a ₹1,000 crore Blackwell term sheet.
origin: E2E Networks incorporated in Delhi in 2009 and grew as a cloud and hosting provider for Indian companies. It listed on the National Stock Exchange and became a MeitY-empanelled cloud platform. As AI demand rose, it shifted toward NVIDIA GPU cloud and its TIR AI/ML platform under managing director Tarun Dua.
today: Larsen & Toubro agreed in November 2024 to buy about 21% of E2E for ₹1,407 crore. In September 2025 E2E won a ₹177 crore IndiaAI Mission order to supply about 1.3 crore H100 and H200 GPU hours over 360 days to the startup Gnani.ai. It launched a 1,024-GPU B200 cluster on its TIR platform in May 2026, hosted at the L&T-Vyoma data center in Chennai. Revenue for Q1 FY27 rose 334% to ₹156.8 crore with a 75.2% EBITDA margin. On August 31, 2026, it signed a binding term sheet worth about ₹1,000 crore with an unnamed Indian sovereign AI company for Blackwell GPU cloud services through June 2029.
platform: E2E sells GPU virtual machines in one to eight GPU configurations, priced from $2.69 an hour for an H100 to $6.99 an hour for a B200, along with managed Kubernetes, object and block storage and databases. TIR, its AI/ML platform, covers training, fine-tuning, inference endpoints and development nodes. The B200 cluster follows an NVIDIA reference architecture with InfiniBand networking.
outlook: E2E plans to buy 2,048 more Blackwell GPUs and targets Vera Rubin systems over the next two to three years. The ₹1,000 crore deal is a term sheet that still needs a definitive agreement and new GPU purchases. E2E holds its Q2 FY27 earnings call on October 16, 2026.

name: Modal
snippet: New York serverless GPU platform that bills by the second. It raised $355M at $4.65B in May 2026, and in September it was reported to be closing $750M at $15.75B.
origin: Erik Bernhardsson, a former Spotify and Better.com engineer, started Modal in New York in 2021 with CTO Akshat Bubna. The company set out to let developers run Python code on cloud CPUs and GPUs without managing servers or clusters. Demand for AI inference and for sandboxes that run AI-generated code made GPUs the core of its business.
today: Modal raised $355M in a Series C in May 2026 led by Redpoint Ventures and General Catalyst, at a $4.65B post-money valuation, up from $1.1B in September 2025. Its annualized revenue passed $300M by May 2026, up from about $60M the previous September. In September 2026 TechCrunch reported that Modal was closing a $750M round led by Accel at a $15.75B valuation. Customers include Cognition, Suno, Ramp and Substack.
platform: Developers define workloads in Python, and Modal runs them in containers on rented GPUs, charging by the second for the time used. It offers NVIDIA GPUs from T4 to B300, plus sandboxes for testing AI-generated code. Modal does not own data centers and buys capacity in bulk from 13 compute providers.
outlook: Modal had not announced the reported $750M round as of October 13, 2026. It competes with Baseten, Fireworks and Fal for inference spending, in a market where TechCrunch notes that margins are thin because compute is expensive. Because it rents all of its compute, its GPU supply depends on its 13 providers.

name: Baseten
snippet: San Francisco inference platform that serves open and custom models on GPUs from about 20 clouds. It raised $1.5B at up to $13B in June 2026 and is reported to be raising again.
origin: Baseten started in San Francisco in 2019 to give machine learning teams tools to deploy and serve models in production. CEO Tuhin Srivastava and his co-founders built it around model deployment, versioning and observability across GPUs in several clouds. As open-weight language models improved, Baseten focused on high-volume inference for AI application companies.
today: Baseten raised $150M in September 2025 at about $2.15B. In January 2026 it raised $300M at $5B in a round co-led by IVP and CapitalG, with Nvidia investing about $150M. In June 2026 it raised $1.5B in a Series F at up to $13B, with some investors priced at $11B, from a group that includes Altimeter, Conviction, Spark Capital, Sands Capital and Wellington Management. Reuters reported that revenue grew 20-fold over the prior year, and Australia's Blackbird made its largest investment to date in the round. In September 2026 Axios reported that Baseten was in talks to raise at a $26B valuation.
platform: Baseten offers Model APIs for popular open models, dedicated deployments for custom and fine-tuned models, and reinforcement learning training through its Loops SDK. Baseten Chains links several models and steps into one workflow with per-step hardware control. Customers run it on Baseten Cloud, in their own VPCs or in a hybrid setup, and dedicated GPUs bill by the minute, from T4 to B200.
outlook: Baseten plans to spend its 2026 funding on more compute capacity, software and hiring. It sources compute from about 20 cloud providers rather than owning data centers. It competes with Fireworks AI and Cerebras in inference, and with the closed model labs' own APIs.

name: Fireworks AI
snippet: Inference platform founded by former Meta PyTorch engineers. It raised $1.5B at $17.5B in July 2026 and reports over $1B in annualized revenue and 40 trillion tokens a day.
origin: Lin Qiao, who led PyTorch engineering at Meta from 2015 to 2022, founded Fireworks in 2022 with five other former Meta engineers. The team set out to serve open models quickly and cheaply on GPUs for developers and enterprises. Cursor became an early customer and used Fireworks to serve its Fast Apply model in 2024.
today: Fireworks raised $250M in a Series C in October 2025 at a $4B valuation, led by Lightspeed, Index Ventures and Evantic. In July 2026 it raised about $1.5B in a Series D at $17.5B, led by Atreides Management, Index Ventures and TCV, with Nvidia participating. Annualized revenue passed $1B by July 2026, up fivefold in a year. Daily volume rose from 15 trillion to more than 40 trillion tokens, and about 95% of those tokens come from customized models.
platform: Fireworks sells serverless per-token inference, dedicated deployments billed by the GPU hour, and reserved capacity. Listed GPU prices run from $8 an hour for an H100 or H200 to $20 an hour for a GB300. It also offers supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning training, and in July 2026 it released Fireworks Nexus, a routing layer that moves routine coding work to open-weight models.
outlook: Fireworks plans to spend the Series D on infrastructure and to grow from about 200 to 600 employees by the end of 2026. In September 2026 The Information reported that it was considering another round. It does not disclose how many GPUs it runs or which clouds supply them.
